lines: I remember the cure flying true when everything else had gone crooked.
You stayed close when I was dangerous to be near.
My hands remembered the fletching table before my mind did.
The hum of a bowstring was the first sound that felt familiar.
I knew I was home when I saw the arrow rack.
Some memories are gone, but I remember who brought me back.
Food tastes right again. I did not know how much I missed that.
Every morning feels a little more like my own life.
You gave me time I thought I had lost.
I can work again, slowly, and that means more than I can say.
The fear returns sometimes. So does the memory of your kindness.
People tell me what happened, and I fit the pieces together.
I slept through a whole night yesterday.
My name came back before most faces did.
I still check my hands when I wake up.
Thank you for treating me like a neighbor even then.
The village sounds ordinary again. That is a wonderful thing.
I owe you more than a bundle of arrows could repay.
Being myself feels strange, but it feels good.
I recognize you now. I am glad I can finally say that.
Your face lands near the target, but the rest of the memory wobbles.
There was a hiss, a bite of gold, and then my thoughts began to settle.
I know your voice, though I cannot place where I heard it.
The workshop light feels familiar. You do too.
Was it you who stayed beside me after the cure?
I remember reaching for the arrow rack before I knew my own name.
Some faces return at once. Yours comes back in pieces.
I woke with your voice caught in one of the gaps.
Did you bring me home, or am I mixing two memories together?
My hands know their work. My mind is still catching up.
The smell of glue brought back an entire morning.
I keep finding familiar places that feel newly built.
Tell me your name once more. I want to keep it this time.
I remember being afraid of you, then safe beside you.
There are days missing between the sickness and this room.
You look kinder than the memory attached to you.
I know I should thank you. I am trying to remember why.
The target lane came back clearly. Everything after it is fog.
Do not take my staring personally. I am sorting out my own life.
Your face is almost where it belongs in my memory.
I remember you, and the memory still makes my hands shake.
I know you helped. Give me room anyway.
The cure worked, but fear does not leave as cleanly.
Do not stand between me and the door.
Your voice brings back parts I would rather forget.
I am grateful. I am also not ready to trust you.
My hands remember reaching for the arrow rack before I could think.
The smell of glue makes that whole room return at once.
I woke safe and still wanted to run.
You did the right thing. That does not make the memory easy.
Please stop asking whether I feel better.
Some mornings I still expect to be sick.
I can speak to you from here. Do not come closer.
People say you saved me. My nerves have not heard them yet.
I need time before your face feels safe again.
The feather pile was the first thing I recognized.
I remember enough to know none of this was simple.
Thank you for the cure. That is all I can give you today.
I am myself again, but not the same as before.
Leave me a clear path out and we can talk.
